failure_case.summary: US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.
US influenza mechanism underpredicted a missed hospitalization peak.

llm_output.why_top_candidate_wins: signal_chile_flu has the strongest combined support (highest score=7) and the richest direct links in the support subgraph. It is the only candidate that both (a) is annotated as a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR the failing target signal_us_hosp and (b) has two mechanistic links to the mechanism eq_us_flu_base (IMPORTATION_LINK and POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF). Those three edges provide a plausible causal pathway by which elevated influenza activity in Chile could precede and seed increased US hospitalizations via importation and by directly driving the base mechanism. By contrast, signal_australia_flu lacks an IMPORTATION_LINK to the mechanism (it only has POSSIBLE_DRIVER_OF + LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR) and signal_travel_pressure lacks a LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR edge to the target; both therefore provide weaker direct support for a missed US peak in hospitalizations than signal_chile_flu.
llm_output.proposed_minimal_edit: Add or activate an importation forcing term from signal_chile_flu into eq_us_flu_base: create/enable an IMPORTATION_INPUT edge (with a short lag parameter) from signal_chile_flu -> eq_us_flu_base that increases seeding/influx to the US transmission process. This minimal mechanism edit leverages the existing IMPORTATION_LINK and LEADING_INDICATOR_FOR evidence to test whether Chile activity explains the underpredicted US hospitalization peak.
llm_output.caveat: This edit is justified by the provided graph links and ranking but does not prove causality; the IMPORTATION_INPUT should be parameterized and fitted (including lag and magnitude) and alternative drivers (e.g., Australia or travel pressure) should be evaluated in follow-up tests. Observational correlation and lead-lag consistency must be checked before committing to structural changes.
